official_measurement_examples.name: Planning-light relevance
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning guidance says artificial lighting should be considered where development increases lighting or is sensitive to existing artificial light; this is a proposal-specific planning consideration, not a universal prohibition.

official_measurement_examples.name: Statutory nuisance distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Artificial light can constitute statutory nuisance under environmental-health law when statutory tests are met, but the nuisance regime is distinct from planning permission and contains exemptions for specified premises.

official_measurement_examples.name: Dark landscape context
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning guidance recognises intrinsically dark landscapes and ecological sensitivity, but dark-sky context does not itself create a parcel-wide automatic refusal without proposal-specific assessment.

official_measurement_examples.name: Bat lighting sensitivity
official_measurement_examples.fact: Natural England standing advice says development lighting near bat habitats can trigger survey and mitigation needs; absence of a bat record is not proof that bats are absent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Mitigation distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Lighting strategies can use siting, shielding, timing, dimming and dark corridors as mitigation; a proposed mitigation strategy is not proof that installed lighting will comply with conditions or licences.

official_measurement_examples.name: Licence separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Protected-species mitigation licensing can be required in addition to planning permission; planning approval does not automatically grant a wildlife licence and a licence does not grant planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Model versus measurement
official_measurement_examples.fact: Predicted lux contours, design calculations or lighting classes are model/design evidence and must not be silently treated as post-installation site measurements at receptors.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Lighting context does not establish ownership, exact buildable area, ecological clearance or final development yield without proposal-specific design, survey and compliance evidence.

core_rules: light pollution is proposal-specific planning consideration
dark landscape is not automatic planning refusal
statutory nuisance is distinct from planning permission
nuisance exemption is not planning approval
predicted lux is not measured lux
lighting design is not installed compliance
bat record absence is not bat absence
wildlife licence is distinct from planning permission
planning permission does not replace species licence
mitigation strategy is not proof of delivery
lighting does not establish land ownership
lighting context does not calculate development yield
ecological lighting constraints require current evidence
no parcel lighting clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
